references.text: Judas gains control of the situation by accepting the bread, just as he accepts what he receives from Jesus, before leaving the room.
Jesus declares that one of the disciples will betray him, which leads directly to Judas' decisive action and flight.
After Satan has entered Judas, he is told to do quickly what he must do, resulting in his immediate departure from the room.
Judas returns with a crowd to arrest Jesus, confirming that he had left the room to fetch them.
The prophecy that a curse will penetrate the enemy like water mirrors Judas' actions and his flight into darkness.
Darkness has not overcome the light, but Judas' departure into the night underscores the dividing line between light and darkness in John's Gospel.
